paper_metadata.title: Traumatic Brain Injury-Related Symptoms Reported by Parents: Clinical, Imaging, and Host Predictors in Children with Impairments in Consciousness Less than 24 Hours

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses a subset of a larger prospective cohort (TRACK-TBI). While the source population and inclusion/exclusion criteria are well-defined, the final sample size is small (n=45) and represents a specific 'pilot' subset, which may limit generalizability to the broader pediatric TBI population.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Children were enrolled within 24 h of injury, after presentation in the emergency department (ED) at one of two Level 1 trauma centers participating in the pediatric pilot.
items.reasoning: The authors clearly define the source (Level 1 trauma centers) and the specific population (pediatric patients with head trauma).

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: Forty-five consecutive eligible patients between three to 16 years of age... were included in this study.
items.reasoning: The use of consecutive recruitment from ED presentations helps minimize selection bias.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: We analyzed a subset of pediatric subjects enrolled in the TRACK-TBI study from March 2014 to March 2017.
items.reasoning: The specific three-year window is explicitly stated.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location) are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: presentation in the emergency department (ED) at one of two Level 1 trauma centers participating in the pediatric pilot.
items.reasoning: The setting (ED) and type of facility (Level 1 trauma centers) are provided.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: Enrolled children were required to have undergone acute neuroimaging (CT or MRI) within 24h of injury... Subjects were excluded if they had spinal cord injury graded as American Spinal Injury Association C or worse, severe extracranial injuries...
items.reasoning: Detailed clinical criteria for both inclusion and exclusion are provided, including the 'zero time' of 24 hours post-injury.

risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Loss to follow-up (from baseline sample to study population analyzed) is not associated with key characteristics (i.e., the study data adequately represent the sample) sufficient to limit potential bias to the observed relationship between PF and outcome.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: Prognostic factors (MRI findings and clinical markers) were measured using standardized Common Data Elements (CDE) and interpreted by expert neuroradiologists/neurosurgeons, ensuring high reliability.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: Neuroimaging findings were then categorized into ''intra-axial'' lesions (CDE defined brain contusion or hemorrhage, diffuse axonal injury, or traumatic axonal injury) and ''extra-axial'' lesions...
items.reasoning: The prognostic factors (lesion types) are explicitly defined using international CDE standards.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: Both clinical and research images were coded using the CDE definitions by a neuroradiologist, pediatric neuroradiologist, and/or a neurosurgeon, with disagreements resolved by consensus.
items.reasoning: The use of multiple expert raters and a consensus process for imaging interpretation ensures high reliability.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: Neuroimaging findings were then categorized into ''intra-axial'' lesions... and ''extra-axial'' lesions...
items.reasoning: The categorization is based on anatomical definitions (CDE) rather than data-driven statistical cut-points.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Overall, 31 cases were coded primarily from the long study scan, eight from the brief study scan, and six from clinical scans.
items.reasoning: While all used MRI, the specific protocols (long vs. brief vs. clinical) varied based on the child's age and ability to cooperate.

items.evidence_snippet: Forty-three of our 45 (96%) subjects completed a two-week study MRI scan.
items.reasoning: The vast majority of the sample had the primary prognostic factor (MRI) measured.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (HBI) is a validated, CDE-recommended tool for pediatric TBI. While parent-report has inherent subjectivity, it is the standard for this age range and was applied consistently.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: parent (or other adult caregiver)-reported TBI-related symptoms were measured via the Health and Behavior Inventory (HBI), a 20-item questionnaire...
items.reasoning: The outcome measure and its subscales (cognitive/somatic) are clearly defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: The HBI was recommended by the CDEs as a core measure of TBI-related symptoms for children across the age and injury spectrum.
items.reasoning: The authors cite the validity of the HBI and its status as a core CDE measure.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: All follow-ups were completed in person, except for the three-month follow-up, which was completed by telephone.
items.reasoning: The protocol for outcome collection was standardized across the cohort for each specific time point.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study adjusted for several key confounders (age, sex, SES, baseline symptoms). However, the small sample size limited the ability to include all potential confounders (like parental stress) in a single comprehensive model.

items.label: Important Confounders Measured

items.evidence_snippet: In each multi-variable model, age, sex, socioeconomic status, and baseline symptom level were controlled...
items.reasoning: Key demographic and clinical confounders were measured, but the authors admit they could not assess environmental factors like parental stress.

items.label: Definition of the confounding factor

items.evidence_snippet: Health insurance was selected as a proxy to reflect one estimate of socioeconomic status. Positive neurobehavioral history was defined as reported history of previously diagnosed...
items.reasoning: The authors provide clear operational definitions for the confounders used in the models.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Confounders
items.prompt: Measurement of all important confounders is adequately valid and reliable (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: at the two-week assessment, parents/caregivers retrospectively rated pre-injury symptoms over the four weeks before injury.
items.reasoning: Baseline symptoms rely on retrospective recall, which is subject to 'recall bias' or 'good-old-days' bias.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The statistical approach was sophisticated, using robust regression to handle the small sample size and outliers. The reporting is transparent regarding the limitations of power and the preliminary nature of the findings.

items.label: Presentation of analytical strategy
items.prompt: There is sufficient presentation of data to assess the adequacy of the analysis.
items.evidence_snippet: To combat the limitation of small sample size, we utilized robust regression models... Cases with Cook distance >1 because of high leverage or high residuals were dropped...
items.reasoning: The analytical strategy is described in detail, including the handling of outliers.

items.label: Model development strategy
items.prompt: The strategy for model building (i.e., inclusion of variables in the statistical model) is appropriate and is based on a conceptual framework or model.
items.evidence_snippet: In each multi-variable model, age, sex, socioeconomic status, and baseline symptom level were controlled, while the main effects of one of the predictors of interest... was investigated.
items.reasoning: The model building strategy (controlling for known covariates while testing specific predictors) is standard and appropriate for the study goals.

items.prompt: The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study.
items.evidence_snippet: we utilized robust regression models, which are less sensitive to outliers and/or influential cases that could bias the results (STATA rreg package).
items.reasoning: Robust regression is an excellent choice for a small clinical sample (n=45) where individual outliers can significantly skew results.

items.label: Reporting of results
items.prompt: There is no selective reporting of results.
items.evidence_snippet: We also did not adjust for multiple testing because of the limited sample size, and acknowledge the resulting increased risk for false positive results.
items.reasoning: The authors are transparent about their findings, including those that did not support their hypotheses, and discuss the risks of their approach.
